Article Title: China hits $1 trillion trade surplus milestone for second year in a row
Article Text:
Representative image

AI demand supports exports, but trade tensions persist

Weak domestic demand adds to export dependence

Oil imports fall despite supply concerns

China's trade surplus crossed $1 trillion in the first 10 months of the year, as strong global demand for high-tech products, fuelled by the race to build artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, helped offset weak domestic consumption.The surplus reached $1.04 trillion between January and October, according to customs data released on Tuesday.China has now recorded a trade surplus of more than $1 trillion for a second consecutive year, reaching the milestone a month earlier than in 2025.Exports rose 35.2% in October from a year earlier in US dollar terms, slightly below September's 36.3% increase but higher than the 33.5% growth forecast by economists in a Reuters poll.Imports grew 41.6%, accelerating from 31% in September and beating the poll's median forecast of 32%.Despite the stronger import growth, China's trade surplus narrowed to $105.3 billion in October from $133.5 billion in September.The export performance reflects China's growing reliance on overseas demand as subdued domestic consumption and a prolonged property market downturn weigh on its economy.The global AI investment boom has supported sales of Chinese technology products, including semiconductors and electronics, but the expanding surplus is also raising concerns among trading partners.Much of China's export growth this year has been driven by the global push to expand AI infrastructure. Analysts expect demand for Chinese technology products to remain strong into 2027, although the outlook will depend on how long the investment boom lasts.“The outlook for exports depends on how long the AI boom will last,” Macquarie analysts wrote, adding that exports could accelerate further in the fourth quarter before beginning to slow from the first quarter of 2027.Dave Chia, an economist at Moody's Analytics, also expects Chinese exports to remain strong through the rest of the year, led by electronics and automobiles.However, the expanding surplus could intensify trade tensions, particularly with the European Union.European leaders have called for further trade restrictions on China after reaching an agreement with Beijing to limit Chinese hybrid vehicle exports to the bloc over the next few years.Since the measures have yet to take effect, manufacturers are expected to bring forward shipments, supporting exports in the near term.“The risk of additional tariffs and other trade barriers will remain elevated in 2027, particularly as Chinese manufacturers continue expanding their presence in overseas markets,” said Joe Peissel, lead macroeconomist at Trivium China.The US-China trade relationship also remains uncertain. Beijing on Monday officially announced a two-month extension of its trade truce with Washington, which was due to expire on November 10.However, China said last week that any expansion of its purchases of US agricultural goods would depend on the implementation of the agreed reciprocal tariff-reduction arrangement.China's trade surplus with the US narrowed slightly to $32.71 billion in October from $34.01 billion in September, but the gap remains a point of friction between the two economies.Trade is expected to feature prominently in the planned meeting between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen later this month.The two leaders are expected to meet for the third time this year.The strong export performance comes against the backdrop of subdued consumer spending in China. A prolonged downturn in the property market has weakened household wealth and confidence, leaving domestic demand under pressure.The weakness has also pushed Chinese manufacturers to look overseas for customers. Automobile exports maintained a solid pace of growth in October, while domestic vehicle sales recorded their 12th consecutive monthly decline, according to separate industry data.AP cited analysts who said overcapacity in several industries, excess domestic savings and weak domestic demand were pushing Chinese companies to sell more goods abroad. Alicia García-Herrero, chief economist for Asia Pacific at Natixis, said the situation was not sustainable.Businesses are also facing intense competition at home. Cinders Zhou, who sells eyewear for a manufacturer in the eastern Chinese city of Linhai, told AP that competition had increasingly centred on price as products across the industry became more similar.“It comes down to product quality, or rather the increasingly the lack of it across the industry, since there's significant homogenization,” Zhou said. “That has forced everyone to compete on price.”Greater dependence on overseas markets also leaves China's economy more exposed to a slowdown in global demand or further trade restrictions. Analysts have warned that any correction in the AI industry could hurt exports of chips and electronics.“If the AI boom slows or turns into a correction, lower chip and electronics prices and smaller shipping volumes would hit China's exports hard,” Chia said, according to AP.China's oil imports fell 13.3% in October compared with a year earlier, although shipments reached their highest level since March as buyers sought supplies following disruptions to Middle East flows caused by the US-Israeli war on Iran.The trade figures come ahead of the APEC summit, where trade policy and tariffs are expected to be among the key issues in discussions between Trump and Xi. The two sides had previously proposed a $60 billion package of reciprocal tariff cuts following their September summit in Washington, including around $17 billion worth of US agricultural goods.While Chinese officials have maintained that Beijing is not seeking to expand its trade surplus and wants more balanced global trade, the latest figures underline the importance of overseas demand to the country's export-led growth.
Article Summary: Exports rose 35.2% in October from a year earlier in US dollar terms, slightly below September's 36.3% increase. Imports grew 41.6%, accelerating from 31% in September and beating the poll's median forecast of 32%. Despite the stronger import growth, China's trade surplus narrowed to $105.3 billion in October.

Article Title: Russia-US diesel deal delivers results? Lavrov claims prices have already fallen
Article Text:
Russia hails diesel deal with US (representative image)

US-bound shipments face uncertainty

Lavrov raises Ukraine strikes on Russian energy infrastructure

Russian foreign minister Sergei Lavrov has said an agreement allowing Russia to resume diesel exports to the United States and global markets is already being implemented and has helped bring prices down.In an article published in Moscow daily Kommersant on Tuesday, Lavrov said the arrangement was an important contribution to energy security. He also argued that Russia did not use its economy to score political points against countries it considered adversaries or competitors.Also Read| Iran war, cost of living drag Trump’s approval rating near career low: Survey “Since 2022, we have supplied Europe with energy resources worth $320 billion,” Lavrov wrote.“An important contribution to energy security was the agreement between the Russian and US leaders to suspend restrictions on the export of Russian diesel. We have already started implementing it, which immediately brought prices down.”US President Donald Trump announced the deal on October 9. Under the arrangement, Russia agreed to make 300,000 metric tonnes, or 2.25 million barrels, of diesel available immediately to the US and global markets, followed by 500,000 tonnes in November and a further 1 million tonnes “immediately thereafter”.The Trump administration temporarily lifted US sanctions on Russian fuel to facilitate the exports.The move came as the US president sought to bring down fuel prices ahead of the November 3 midterm elections, which his Republican Party lost.Lavrov did not provide figures to support his claim that the agreement had lowered diesel prices.US diesel futures have fallen about 11% since the deal was announced, according to Reuters.However, diesel prices at US pumps were at a record high last week when Americans voted, according to price tracker GasBuddy.The arrangement has also faced uncertainty over whether Russian fuel would reach the US.Two sanctioned tankers that had initially declared destinations on the US East Coast changed course, while a third vessel travelling across the North Atlantic changed its destination from New York to “for orders”, according to news agency AP.The report said the proposed imports had yet to result in a confirmed US delivery. Analysts also questioned whether the shipments would reach American ports, citing regulatory and sanctions-related concerns.New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill had advised port and terminal operators in the state to reject Russian fuel shipments, warning of possible legal consequences. A bipartisan group of US senators also urged Trump to abandon the arrangement, arguing that it could provide financial support to Moscow.The US Treasury Department, however, maintained that its temporary authorisation for Russian diesel transactions was consistent with previous actions and “in compliance with all applicable laws”.The exemption was issued for the sale, delivery, unloading and import of Russian diesel until April 7.Separately, Russian deputy foreign minister Alexander Pankin said on Monday that the diesel arrangement could provide an opportunity for the gradual restoration of business and other ties between Moscow and Washington.He told the TASS state news agency that the deal could “serve as a foundation for the gradual restoration of business and other ties between our countries”.In his Kommersant article, Lavrov said Russia was working to stabilise global energy markets and ensure energy security, as well as the balanced and sustainable development of countries and regions.He also accused Ukraine of ignoring Trump's calls to stop attacks on Russian energy infrastructure.Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said last week that Kyiv's forces were continuing their strikes.Russian media have reported that fuel shortages have returned in at least half a dozen Russian regions following Ukrainian attacks on at least eight major oil refineries over the past two weeks.
Article Summary: Russian foreign minister Sergei Lavrov hails diesel deal with US. Deal allows Russia to resume diesel exports to the United States and global markets. US President Donald Trump announced the deal on October 9. The arrangement has faced uncertainty over whether Russian fuel would reach the US.

Article Title: Oil prices today: Crude edges lower as Donald Trump signals pause in military action against Iran
Article Text:
Crude oil eases (representative image)

Trump signals pause in strikes, but Hormuz blockade to continue

Opec output rises, Russia-Ukraine talks in focus

Oil prices edged lower on Tuesday, extending the previous session's losses, after US President Donald Trump said military action against Iran was not necessary “at this point”. His remarks eased concerns over prolonged disruptions to oil supplies from the Middle East.Brent crude futures fell 24 cents, or 0.23%, to $92.33 a barrel by 0102 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures declined 35 cents, or 0.40%, to $86.50 a barrel.Brent had settled 5.85% lower in the previous session after falling to its lowest level since August 31.Trump said on Monday that he planned to hold off on fresh military strikes against Iran for the time being, following appeals from countries in the region. These included an appeal from Qatar's prime minister during talks at the White House.In an interview with Reuters and a subsequent appearance in the White House briefing room, Trump said the US would maintain its naval blockade in the Strait of Hormuz for now.“The market continues to prioritise President Trump's more conciliatory tone toward Iran since the midterms,” said Tim Waterer, chief market analyst at KCM Trade.He added that attacks on shipping around the Strait of Hormuz were continuing but had not escalated enough to bring a fresh risk premium into the market.However, senior US and Gulf officials have expressed doubts about the possibility of an imminent peace deal between Washington and Tehran.Iranian security council chief Mohsen Rezaei rejected reports of negotiations, saying the US should “stop manufacturing fake news about imaginary talks”.He added that it was “time to surrender to the seven conditions Iran has repeatedly set out”.On the supply side, oil production by the Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (Opec) increased in October, according to a Reuters survey. The rise was led by higher output in Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and Iraq, despite continued constraints on exports.Elsewhere, Russian and Ukrainian officials were scheduled to meet on Tuesday for two days of US-brokered talks. The meeting would be their first since February.Trump had suggested last week that a broader peace agreement could be possible in the 4.5-year-old Russia-Ukraine war and could also incorporate Europe's security.
Article Summary: Brent crude futures fell 0.23%, to $92.33 a barrel by 0102 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures declined 35 cents, to $86.50 a barrel. Trump said he planned to hold off on fresh military strikes against Iran for the time being.

Article Title: Stock market holiday today: Are NSE, BSE open or closed on November 10 for Diwali-Balipratipada? Check details
Article Text:
Stock market open or closed on Nov 10?

Are NSE and BSE closed?

The festive season has brought changes to the regular trading schedule, with Indian stock exchanges observing holidays around Diwali. After a special Muhurat Trading session on Sunday and a regular trading session on Monday, investors may be looking to resume trading on Tuesday, November 10.According to the 2026 holiday calendar of the National Stock Exchange (NSE) and the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE), will remain closed on account of Diwali-Balipratipada. The holiday applies to the equity, equity derivatives and securities lending and borrowing (SLB) segments, among other market segments.Sensex and Nifty ended higher on Monday, recovering after marginally slipping in the special Muhurat trading session on Sunday. The Sensex rose 107.25 points, or 0.13 per cent, to 81,106.65, while the Nifty gained 58.25 points, or 0.23 per cent, to reclaim the 25,000 mark at 25,044.65. Buying in banking and financial stocks, along with a decline in crude oil prices, supported the benchmarks, although losses in IT and metal shares capped gains. Brent crude fell 1.04 per cent to $97.46 per barrel.Also read: Are banks open or closed on November 10, 2026? Check state-wise list Yes. Both the NSE and BSE will remain closed on Tuesday, November 10, for Diwali-Balipratipada.Trading will remain suspended across the equity, equity derivatives and SLB segments. The capital market, derivatives market, electronic gold receipts (EGR) and debt market will also remain closed.The exchanges will resume normal trading on Wednesday, November 11, with the regular equity market session scheduled from 9:15 am to 3:30 pm.Meanwhile, the Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX) will remain closed during the morning session, from 9 am to 5 pm. However, trading will resume in the evening session from 5 pm to 11:30 pm.The National Commodity and Derivatives Exchange (NCDEX), meanwhile, will remain closed for the entire day.The exchanges have declared November 10 a trading holiday on account of Diwali-Balipratipada, also known as Bali Pratipada. The festival is observed on the day after Diwali and marks the annual return of King Mahabali to his kingdom, according to Hindu mythology.The holiday follows the special Muhurat Trading session held on Sunday, November 8, to mark the beginning of Samvat 2083, the Hindu financial year. The exchanges subsequently conducted a regular trading session on Monday, November 9.After the November 10 closure, the next scheduled trading holiday for the NSE and BSE is November 24, Tuesday, on account of Prakash Gurpurb Sri Guru Nanak Dev.The exchanges will also remain closed on December 25 for Christmas, according to their 2026 holiday calendars, apart from the regular weekend holidays.
Article Summary: NSE and BSE will remain closed on Tuesday, November 10, for Diwali- Balipratipada. The holiday applies to the equity, equity derivatives and securities lending and borrowing (SLB) segments. The capital market, derivatives market, electronic gold receipts (EGR) and debt market will also remain closed.

Article Title: Will probe into Nvidia's Jensen Huang indirectly benefit Indian stock markets?
Article Text:
Nvidia announced the probe on Sunday, following Huang's admission that he had been intimate with a business executive. (Image for representative purpose only)

What has happened

Does it impact India?

(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India.)

Nvidia, one of the most valuable listed companies in the world, is in the eye of the storm with the company launching an investigation into reports that its chief executive, Jensen Huang, had been the “target of a foreign intelligence effort. ” Nvidia shares dropped 8% at the start of trading on Monday.Nvidia's processors are widely used in data centres and computing infrastructure that train and operate AI models. Its most advanced chips have also come under the spotlight because of US export curbs designed to restrict China's access to cutting-edge semiconductor technology.Nvidia announced the probe on Sunday, following Huang's admission that he had been intimate with a business executive whom US intelligence agencies had reportedly identified as someone collecting information for China, according to The New York Times.The New York Times identified Alice Huang as a former executive at Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based data centre company whose website prominently highlights its partnership with Nvidia.Nvidia ranks among the world's most valuable publicly listed companies, alongside Apple and Microsoft. Its chip sales to China have periodically faced restrictions from US regulators seeking to curb Beijing's access to advanced technology.“The key questions are whether he was aware of any espionage activities and whether any confidential or strategically sensitive information was compromised,” said George Chen, a partner and chair of digital practice at The Asia Group, a Washington-based consultancy according to AP report.“Those questions require evidence rather than speculation,” he added in a text message to reporters.In recent years, Huang has pressed Washington to ease restrictions on Nvidia's chip exports to China. This year, he secured US President Donald Trump's approval to sell the company's H200 chips to the country. However, it remains uncertain whether Beijing will permit Chinese companies to purchase these processors in substantial volumes.In a regulatory filing in August, Nvidia disclosed that it had sold only a limited quantity of chips to China, citing restrictions imposed by the Chinese government on such purchases.Although the H200 is not among Nvidia's most advanced chip models, it remains a sophisticated processor. Huang had earlier also lobbied Trump for permission to sell the company's less advanced H20 chips, which were specifically designed to comply with US export restrictions on China.China's Foreign Ministry rejected the espionage allegations on Monday, describing them as a smear campaign directed at Beijing.The development has plunged the US chipmaker, a key player in the global artificial intelligence industry, into an unprecedented crisis.The company also lacks a clearly identified successor to its chief executive.The more serious concern is the allegation that Huang “has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.”Nvidia's board has launched an investigation and maintained that it has “no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised.”The controversy has surfaced at a particularly difficult moment for the company.Democrats secured control of Congress last week, while candidates advocating closer oversight of artificial intelligence and data-centre construction recorded significant victories.Nvidia was already facing the possibility of tougher congressional scrutiny over whether its advanced chips were reaching China. The latest allegations involving Huang have given lawmakers from both parties further grounds to examine the company.One would assume that an internal probe in a tech giant in the US would have no impact whatsoever on Indian stock markets.But, Sensex and Nifty which have delivered negative returns in the last year may actually benefit indirectly from this development. Globally stock markets have rallied on the artificial intelligence and chip-led boom with Nvidia actually leading the rally.India on the other hand has missed out on the AI stock boom, one of the major factors cited for exit of foreign investors from the stock market.But after months of underperformance, Indian equities have recently regained investor interest as concerns grow over concentrated investments in AI. Investors are increasingly looking towards factors such as lower crude oil prices and robust domestic corporate earnings. Last week, India emerged as one of Asia's most prominent beneficiaries of the so-called anti-AI trade.The positive sentiment towards Indian equities received another boost on Monday, with two more banks turning bullish on the market. HSBC upgraded Indian stocks to overweight from neutral, while Citigroup increased its 12-month target for the Nifty 50.Nvidia is at the heart of the AI investment boom and has increasingly relied on its own balance sheet and credit strength to support faster infrastructure spending.Bloomberg Opinion columnist Shuli Ren has described Huang as the “central banker of AI.” The question she raises is particularly relevant now: Will Nvidia's money keep flowing now that the central banker himself is in trouble?According to a Bloomberg analysis, while Huang's troubles alone are not a sufficient basis for an investment case for India, but if the controversy deepens doubts about the AI trade and prompts investors to diversify beyond it, Indian equities could benefit from an unusual advantage that the country does not have a giant, expensive AI sector.
Article Summary: N Nvidia, one of the most valuable listed companies in the world, is in the eye of the storm. The company has launched an investigation into reports that its chief executive, Jensen Huang, had been the “target of a foreign intelligence effort” Nvidia shares dropped 8% at the start of trading on Monday.

Article Title: $69.3 billion IPO? Anthropic shares price details with banks, then retracts
Article Text:
Anthropic is planning its market debut under symbol "ANT"

Anthropic's proposed initial public offering (IPO), which could have raised nearly $70 billion, was briefly outlined in a securities filing circulated to banks before the artificial intelligence company retracted the pricing details.An Anthropic representative sent bankers a copy of a filing showing plans to offer around 867 million shares at a price range of $70 to $80 apiece. The company subsequently sent another email saying the pricing information was inaccurate and that an updated filing would follow, reported Reuters.Anthropic did not specify which details were incorrect as there has been no public confirmation around this.The original email, cited by Reuters, indicated that the proposed offering would involve 866.7 million Class A shares, including around 843.3 million shares sold by Anthropic and 23.3 million shares offered by existing shareholders. At the top of the proposed price range, the IPO could have raised $69.3 billion.The original filing also showed that Anthropic had lined up a separate private placement worth $26 billion, involving some of the world's biggest technology companies. Alphabet's Google, Nvidia, Advanced Micro Devices, Broadcom, Micron Technology, Microsoft and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) had agreed to participate by purchasing Anthropic's Class N common stock at the IPO price.The private placement was to close immediately after the public offering.Anthropic is expected to formally launch its IPO roadshow on Tuesday, with pricing expected the following week.The proposed listing comes as Anthropic seeks to capitalise on growing demand for generative AI and its Claude family of models. Founded in 2021 by former OpenAI executives, including chief executive Dario Amodei and his sister Daniela Amodei, the company has emerged as one of the leading players in the AI industry.In its IPO disclosures, Anthropic said it planned to list on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol ANT. However, the number of shares to be offered and the price range had not been finalised, based on public information.Anthropic reported revenue of $16.3 billion in the first half of 2026, alongside a net loss of $80.7 billion. A substantial portion of the reported loss was linked to changes in the fair value of convertible notes, derivative liabilities and other financing instruments, rather than being a direct measure of operating cash expenditure.The company expects significant spending to continue as it invests in computing infrastructure, research, AI safety and expansion. Its disclosures also warn that it may not achieve or sustain profitability.The filing outlined risks associated with the development of advanced AI systems, including the possibility that they could pose catastrophic or existential threats to humanity without adequate safeguards and oversight. It also highlighted risks arising from misuse, autonomous capabilities and the possibility that AI research could advance faster than the ability to evaluate and secure new models.Anthropic's IPO comes amid growing scrutiny of the enormous capital requirements of the AI industry. Several companies in the AI infrastructure and data centre sectors have delayed or withdrawn planned listings, while concerns over interest rates and the sustainability of AI spending have weighed on companies such as CoreWeave.Investors had previously discussed a valuation of as much as $2 trillion for Anthropic, although expectations have since moderated, with $1.5 trillion viewed as the upper end of the range, Reuters had reported.The company's growth has been supported by major technology partners, particularly Google and Amazon, which are also investors, computing infrastructure providers and distribution partners. Anthropic has nearly $900 billion in computing commitments with partners including the two companies, highlighting its dependence on substantial future infrastructure capacity.
Article Summary: Anthropic sent bankers a copy of a filing showing plans to offer around 867 million shares at a price range of $70 to $80 apiece. The company subsequently sent another email saying the pricing information was inaccurate. At the top of the proposed price range, the IPO could have raised $69.3 billion.

Article Title: Man sold two properties for Rs 47.54 lakh and received cash payments for them; he paid capital gains tax, yet faced penalty, but ITAT Cuttack cancels it because tax officer invoked wrong section
Article Text:
After examining the facts, ITAT Cuttack held that Section 269SS did not apply to the transactions. (Image for representative purpose only)

What the case is about:

Why did the taxpayer win the case?

What if you sell properties but receive the payment in cash? Despite recording capital gains in your tax return, are you still likely to face penalties from the Income Tax Department The Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT), Cuttack, has ruled in favour of a taxpayer who was penalised for accepting cash from the sale of properties, despite having declared the transactions in his income tax return and paid the applicable capital gains tax.The case concerned a man in Odisha who, according to the submissions before the tribunal, sold two properties for a combined consideration of around Rs 47.54 lakh. However, for this sale he received the entire amount in cash. The person in question disclosed the property transactions in his income tax return (ITR) and paid the capital gains tax due on the sales.The Income Tax Department's Centralised Processing Centre (CPC) in Bengaluru processed his return and accepted his computation of capital gains tax.However, the Assessing Officer (AO) in Berhampur, Odisha, subsequently received information indicating that the man had collected the Rs 47.54 lakh sale proceeds in cash. The AO initiated an investigation, which established that the taxpayer had accepted cash payments for the property transactions.The AO then invoked Section 269SS, read with Sections 271D and 273D, and held that receiving the sale consideration in cash amounted to a violation of Section 269SS, according to an ET report.A penalty was consequently imposed on the man who challenged it before the Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals), or CIT(A).However, the appeal was rejected. He then approached the ITAT in Cuttack, where he secured a favourable ruling on October 5, 2026.The man’s counsel argued that the assessing officer had invoked the wrong section of the Income-tax Act to impose a penalty for accepting cash against the sale of property. He also cited a decision by a coordinate bench of ITAT Cuttack in the case of Satyabrata Panda, dated March 16, 2026, in which the penalty had been cancelled under similar circumstances.After examining the facts, ITAT Cuttack held that Section 269SS did not apply to the transactions for which the AO had sought to impose a penalty under Section 271D. The tribunal also referred to the decision in Satyabrata Panda and noted that a similar issue had arisen in the case of Arati Saraf, where the AO had relied on an incorrect provision of the Income-tax Act to levy a penalty.The tribunal concluded that the AO should have invoked Section 269ST rather than Section 269SS. Since the penalty had been imposed under Section 271D on the basis of the latter provision, ITAT Cuttack cancelled it.However, the cancellation of the Section 271D penalty does not mean that the tribunal declared the cash receipt exempt from all other provisions of the Income-tax Act.Pranshu G, Partner at Ashok Pranshu & Co, told ET that the taxpayer succeeded because the ITAT, Cuttack, considered the cash to be the sale consideration received upon completion of the property transaction, rather than an advance covered by Section 269SS.On this basis, the tribunal set aside the penalty imposed under Section 271D. It held that Section 269ST and the corresponding penalty provision, Section 271DA, were the relevant provisions in the circumstances of the case.Pranshu explained that the matter concerned penalty proceedings and did not involve prosecution. He also pointed out that the Income Tax Department could potentially initiate fresh proceedings against the man under the applicable provision. However, any such move would have to take into account the limitation period prescribed under Section 275.According to Pranshu, courts have differed on whether the requisite satisfaction must be recorded during assessment proceedings before a penalty can be initiated. He added that the Income Tax Department cannot use a change in the applicable statutory provision to revive proceedings for which the limitation period has already expired.Pranshu advises property sellers who have received payments in cash to disclose the entire sale consideration without delay, calculate their capital gains accurately and pay the applicable tax along with interest. They should also check whether they remain eligible to file a revised or updated income tax return for the relevant year.

The person in question disclosed the property transactions in his income tax return (ITR) and paid the capital gains tax due on the sales. However, the Assessing Officer (AO) in Berhampur, Odisha, subsequently received information indicating that the man had collected the sale proceeds in cash. Article Title: Asian stocks today: Markets rally as Wall Street rebounds, oil prices ease on Iran de-escalation hopes
Article Text:
Asian stocks opened higher on Tuesdayfollowing gains in US equities

Wall Street rebound and easing oil prices lift sentiment

Nvidia shares remain under pressure, US inflation data in focus

Asian stocks advanced on Tuesday, extending a recovery in global markets after Wall Street recorded its strongest single-day gain since April. A decline in oil prices following US President Donald Trump's decision to hold off on fresh military strikes against Iran also lifted investor sentiment.Japan's benchmark Nikkei 225 rose 2.6% to 60,279.37, while South Korea's Kospi climbed 4% to 5,219.37.Taiwan's Taiex gained 3.4%. Hong Kong's Hang Seng advanced 0.4% to 24,535.74, and the Shanghai Composite edged 0.4% higher to 3,673.54.Australia's S&P/ASX 200 rose 1.1% to 9,131.70. Meanwhile, MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan was up 1.5% in early trading, according to Reuters.Technology stocks led gains across several markets. Shares in SoftBank Group, an investor in OpenAI, jumped 15% ahead of its earnings announcement. Tokyo Electron rose 5.6%, while Advantest gained 3.4%.In South Korea, Samsung Electronics climbed 4.6% and SK Hynix advanced 5.6%. AFP also reported gains in Taiwan's technology sector, with chipmaker TSMC rising more than 1% and MediaTek gaining over 7%.The rally in Asia followed a strong session on Wall Street on Monday. Article Title: US, China drink less, India pours more
Article Text:
Alcohol consumption volumes in the country jumped 10% in the first half of 2026, the fastest growth among 21 major markets tracked by drinks research firm IWSR

BENGALURU:

TOI

TOI

The world’s two biggest alcohol markets are drinking less, but India seems to be in the mood for another round. Alcohol consumption volumes in the country jumped 10% in the first half of 2026, the fastest growth among 21 major markets tracked by drinks research firm IWSR, according to estimates shared exclusively withIndia was also the only country among these markets where consumption increased across every category and subcategory tracked by IWSR. From beer and whisky to vodka, gin and wine, Indians consumed more of almost everything, even as the wider global drinks industry struggled with falling demand.Beer led the growth, with full-strength beer consumption rising 16% year-on-year during January-June. Ready-to-drink (RTD) alcoholic beverages, which include premixed cocktails and other packaged drinks, grew 12%, while Indian whisky, one of the country’s largest spirits categories, recorded 4% growth.Blended Scotch whisky volumes rose 8%, while vodka and gin grew 6% each. Rum and non-Cognac brandy recorded 3% growth apiece. Still wine consumption increased 2%, while fortified wine grew 7%.Interestingly, the fastest growth among the major subcategories for which IWSR shared India-specific figures came from beer without the booze. No-alcohol beer consumption surged 25%, outpacing every major alcoholic drink category in percentage terms.The numbers stand in sharp contrast to trends elsewhere. Across the 21 markets covered by IWSR, which account for 76% of global beverage alcohol consumption, total volumes fell 1% in the first half of 2026.The US, the world’s largest alcohol market alongside China, recorded a 4% decline in consumption, while China saw volumes fall 3%. Beer consumption declined 4% in the US and 2% in China, compared with India’s 16% growth.Remove the US and China from the calculations, however, and alcohol consumption across the remaining markets actually grew 1%.India topped the growth charts, followed by Colombia at 9%, South Africa at 5%, Brazil at 3% and the UK at 2%. Mexico and Thailand also reported growth, although IWSR did not specify the rates.“India continues to be one of the most important markets for the beverage alcohol industry worldwide. This latest data just reinforces this narrative. Global brands that want to expand internationally are increasingly looking to India as a key source of their growth plans,” said Marten Lodewijks, president and managing director of IWSR, toldThe contrast is visible across individual drinks too. While still wine consumption declined 4% across the 21 markets, it grew 2% in India. No-alcohol beer volumes increased 8% across these markets, compared with India’s 25% rise.IWSR said growing moderation trends and the use of GLP-1 weight-loss drugs were putting pressure on alcohol consumption globally. Inflation, tariffs and economic uncertainty have also weighed on US consumers, while China’s slowing economy and other structural challenges have affected demand.The overall decline across the 21 markets, however, was less severe than a year earlier, when alcohol consumption volumes had fallen 2% in the corresponding six-month period. For the global drinks industry, India’s growing appetite stands out at a time when its two biggest markets are losing their thirst.
Article Summary: Alcohol consumption volumes in the country jumped 10% in the first half of 2026, the fastest growth among 21 major markets tracked by drinks research firm IWSR. Beer led the growth, with full-strength beer consumption rising 16% year-on-year during January-June.

Article Title: Easier GST input tax credit norms increase cash flow by up to 2%
Article Text:
Easier GST input tax credit norms increase cash flow by up to 2%

To help reduce cost

NEW DELHI: The change in input tax credit mechanism introduced by govt has helped generate as much as 2% cash for certain manufacturing sectors, helping lower cost, which has not been passed on to consumers. In the services sector too, tax experts said, businesses have gained due to refunds from ITC on rentals, which can constitute up to 10-15% of the cost for IT and consulting firms.In Sept 2025, the rate rationalisation had reduced several mass consumption items, such as all food products, into the 5% slab from 12% or 18% earlier. The GST Council had also allowed faster provisional refunds for inverted duty cases. At last month's meeting, the Council also allowed refunds on GST paid on input services, giving businesses extra cash flow and reducing overall costs by freeing up working capital."Whether the benefit reaches consumers is only one part of the story. The broader significance of the change lies in reducing the tax and working-capital burden on Indian manufacturing. As India expands its FTA network and integrates more deeply with global value chains, correcting inverted duty structures and rationalising Customs tariffs will become increasingly important to keeping domestic industry competitive.The direction of reform is therefore moving towards a common objective: lower tax friction, unlock working capital and give Indian businesses greater room to invest, scale and compete. In the end, the success of these reforms will depend not merely on how much credit is released, but on how industry puts that money to work and how much value ultimately flows back to the consumer," said Saurabh Agarwal, Tax Partner at EY India.The calculation done by experts showed the impact varies across sectors (see graphic). Unlike last year, when there was a nudge from govt to pass on the benefits to consumers and spur demand, this time there is no similar push. Businesses have pocketed the gain and reversed the benefit for consumers that flowed from last year's tax cuts, citing higher costs. "If you look at the prices, several products are back at last year's level, despite tax rate falling from 28% to 18% or from 12% or 18% to 5%. Tax as a part of the overall price for consumers are very low now," said another consultant.
Article Summary: In Sept 2025, the rate rationalisation had reduced several mass consumption items, such as all food products, into the 5% slab from 12% or 18% earlier. In the services sector too, tax experts said, businesses have gained due to refunds from ITC on rentals.

Article Title: In Noel's crosshairs, Chandra, Mehli reconnect at Tata HQ
Article Text:
In Noel's crosshairs, Chandra, Mehli reconnect at Tata HQ

MUMBAI: Fresh from Italy, where Tata Motors announced the acquisition of commercial vehicle maker Iveco, Tata Sons chairman N Chandrasekaran invited Mehli Mistry, the late Ratan Tata 's confidant and a trustee of the Tata Education and Development Trust, to Bombay House on Thursday.Coming just days after the two were seen together at the wedding celebrations of Mehli's daughter Laila, the meeting reinforced a belief within Tata circles that relations between the two are improving after more than a year marked by a broader power shift within the Tata Group following the death of Ratan Tata.People familiar with the matter said Chandrasekaran and Mehli, who was voted out of the two principal trusts that hold majority in Tata Sons by Noel Tata and others, discussed issues that had affected their ties. Mehli's challenge against his removal is pending before the Maharashtra Charity Commissioner.Mehli and Chandrasekaran's conversation last week was focused on rebuilding trust and restoring a working equation. Mehli later left for Dubai, with both sides appearing keen to move beyond a difficult period in one of Tata Group's most significant internal relationships.For much of the past decade, Mehli and Chandrasekaran were regarded as allies.After the dramatic ouster of Cyrus Mistry as chairman of Tata Sons in 2016, Mehli played a key role in the legal fight that followed between Cyrus and Ratan Tata. When Ratan Tata had to choose a successor, he picked Chandrasekaran, assisted by Mehli. Mehli later backed Chandrasekaran's second and third terms as chairman of Tata Sons. The third term, however, became contentious after Noel Tata, who succeeded Ratan Tata as chairman of Tata Trusts, opposed Chandrasekaran's reappointment.Mehli and Chandrasekaran's relationship survived differences in personality and style. Those who know Mehli describe him as intensely loyal, fiercely independent and refreshingly blunt. Friends admire his willingness to say in a room what others prefer to whisper outside it. Critics point to a temperament that can run ahead of diplomacy. The redeeming feature, according to people who have worked closely with him, is that his anger rarely lingers.Chandrasekaran is a different kind of leader. Publicly measured and understated, he has cultivated the image of a consensus-builder since arriving at Bombay House. Yet colleagues say beneath that calm exterior lies a highly competitive executive with sharp political instincts and an acute understanding of institutional power.Then came the post-Ratan Tata era. Ratan Tata's death in Oct 2024 altered the balance of influence within Tata Trusts, the largest shareholder of Tata Sons. Disagreements that had previously been settled privately soon surfaced within the trusts. Mehli and fellow Tata Trusts trustees Darius Khambata, Pramit Jhaveri and Jehangir Jehangir argued that information on Tata Sons covered under Article 121 of the company's Articles of Association had not been shared with them, limiting their ability to take informed decisions. The four trustees voted Vijay Singh off the Tata Sons board.Concerns about the emerging situation prompted a visit to Delhi by Noel, Tata Trusts vice-chairman Venu Srinivasan, Khambata and Chandrasekaran, who briefed senior government officials on governance issues within the trusts.Mehli, who was inducted into Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT) and Sir Ratan Tata Trust (SRTT) by Ratan Tata and remained one of his most trusted advisers, increasingly found himself at odds with the emerging power structure. He was eventually voted out of the two trusts by Noel, Srinivasan and Singh, who is also a vice-chairman of the trusts.The impasse followed restrictions imposed by the MCC on SRTT, preventing it from joining SDTT in nominating a joint representative for quorum purposes.
Article Summary: Mehli Mistry, the late Ratan Tata's confidant and a trustee of the Tata Education and Development Trust, met Tata Sons chairman N Chandrasekaran at Bombay House. The meeting reinforced a belief within Tata circles that relations between the two are improving after more than a year.

Article Title: Promoters now own 42% of NSE-listed companies, a 3-year high
Article Text:
Promoters now own 42% of NSE-listed cos, a 3-year high

MUMBAI: The total shareholding of private promoters in NSE-listed companies has been moving northwards for the last two quarters, and at nearly 42%, it is now at a three-year high. The rise in aggregate holding by these promoters came after a secular fall in their holding from Dec 2021 till March 2026, an analysis by an arm of Prime Database showed. A rising promoter shareholding trend often indicates that the market is bottoming out.The analysis by primeinfobase.com also showed that the share of mutual funds (MFs) in companies listed on NSE reached yet another all-time high of 11.8% on Sept 30 this year, up from 11.6% on June 30, its 13th consecutive quarter of rise.According to Pranav Haldea, MD, Prime Database Group, this is a further sign of individual investors being convinced that mutual funds are the right investment vehicle for them. In the MF space, over the past several years, monthly gross inflows into various schemes of fund houses have been on a rising trend with the current figure at about Rs 31,000 crore, taking the latest monthly average over the last year to about Rs 30,000 crore.Haldea feels that despite markets being broadly range-bound over the last couple of years, it will be interesting to see if retail investors would continue their faith in mutual funds and keep pumping in about Rs 30,000 crore on a monthly basis through systematic investment plans (SIPs).In contrast to the rise in holdings by mutual funds, as on Sept 30, the share of foreign institutional investors (FIIs) in Indian companies further declined to a 14-year low of 15.6%, from 15.9% the previous quarter.MFs raising their stakes in Indian companies consistently and FIIs cutting back also led to narrowing the holdings-level gap between foreign funds and domestic fund houses. As of Sept 30, this gap was 3.8%.
Article Summary: Promoters now own 42% of NSE-listed cos, a 3-year high. A rising promoter shareholding trend often indicates that the market is bottoming out. The share of mutual funds in companies listed on NSE reached yet another all-time high of 11.8% on Sept 30.

Article Title: Eggs and chicken may cost 25-30% more by December; eggs could hit Rs 8 per piece and without skin dressed chicken Rs 275 per kg as maize and broken rice prices surge
Article Text:
Cost of poultry feed ingredients, including maize and broken rice, has climbed 30-45%. (Image for representative purpose only)

Eggs , chicken to get costlier as feed prices go up

Your meal costs may go up in December as egg and chicken prices could rise by 25-30%. This is because the cost of poultry feed ingredients, including maize and broken rice, has climbed 30-45% over the past month compared with the same period a year ago.Maize and broken rice prices have doubled in the past year. With farmers and traders holding back maize stocks, the industry that uses the grain as a key raw material expects the upward price trend to continue through December.Wholesale egg prices, currently hovering at Rs 6-7 per egg, are projected to climb to Rs 7-8 by December. The wholesale rate of dressed chicken without skin is also expected to rise from the current Rs 225-250 per kg to Rs 260-275 per kg over the same period, according to senior industry executives.December and January are among the busiest months for poultry consumption, with demand typically rising during the Christmas and New Year festivities.Maize, which cost around Rs 18 per kg last year, is now selling at Rs 34 per kg. Prices were in the range of Rs 26-27 per kg just a month ago, according to an ET report.Industry participants fear that the rate could reach Rs 40 per kg by December, as intermediaries in the supply chain stockpile the commodity in anticipation of further price increases.Broken rice has also become significantly more expensive. Its price, which stood at Rs 14-15 per kg around November 2025, has risen to Rs 31-32 per kg. A month ago, it was available at approximately Rs 22-23 per kg, according to trade data.Industry estimates suggest that a deficient monsoon in Maharashtra and Karnataka, two important kharif maize-producing states, could lead to a 15-16% decline in India's kharif maize output."Earlier, whenever prices of maize and rice increased, we used to shift to other cereals like jowar, bajra, ragi etc. However, even these cereals are expensive to use in poultry feed now," KG Anand, general manager of Venkateshwara Hatcheries told the financial daily."Although the increase in production costs has been high, we cannot pass the entire increase in costs to the consumers," said Anand."This year, we are expecting the production to fall by more than 20% during December and January as farmers are likely to sell younger birds in order to reduce the cost of feeding them," said Anand.Maize prices have continued to rise amid a growing diversion of the grain towards ethanol production. Rice prices, meanwhile, have been climbing as the deficient monsoon is expected to weigh on output of the kharif paddy crop.
Article Summary: Cost of poultry feed ingredients, including maize and broken rice, has climbed 30-45% over the past month compared with the same period a year ago. With farmers and traders holding back maize stocks, the industry that uses the grain as a key raw material expects the upward price trend to continue.

Article Title: Woman visited bank to access locker, but found it surrendered without knowledge despite rent payments; commission orders bank to pay Rs 47 lakh for missing jewellery, 6% interest and Rs 3.5 lakh costs
Article Text:
The commission rejected the bank’s contention that the locker had been surrendered on May 21, 2005. (AI image for representative purpose)

What the case is about

Why the commission ruled in favour of locker holder

What documents should you preserve for your bank locker?

Can your bank locker be surrendered without you being aware? And is the bank liable then for items you claim were in the locker that was surrendered without your knowledge?In one such case, a woman who tried to access a joint locker was told by the concerned bank that the locker had already been surrendered.Now, the Delhi State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has directed the bank to pay her compensation for the jewellery she said was missing, along with interest, and mental agony and harassment, and litigation costs.The commission found that the bank had failed to produce records establishing that the locker had been properly surrendered or that its contents had been returned. It rejected the bank’s claim that the locker had been surrendered several years ago, noting that locker rent continued to be debited even years later.A woman held a joint locker with her father-in-law at a bank in Delhi. According to the complaint, the locker arrangement dated back to 1998. Her father-in-law, who operated the locker in 2005, died on August 29, 2010.On September 1, 2018, the woman approached the bank to access the locker. She alleged that the bank informed her it had been surrendered on January 22, 2015. She maintained that she had never requested its surrender and had received no notice that the locker had been closed or allotted to another customer.The woman claimed that jewellery worth approximately Rs 47 lakh was missing from the locker. Alleging deficiency in banking services, she filed a consumer complaint in 2019, seeking the value of the jewellery with interest, compensation for mental agony and litigation expenses.The bank disputed her allegations. In its written statement, it claimed that the locker had been surrendered on May 21, 2005. It described the continued deduction of locker rent as a bona fide mistake and argued that it accepted only empty lockers when customers surrendered them. It also challenged the commission’s jurisdiction and maintained that the complaint was time-barred.The commission first rejected the bank’s jurisdictional objections. It noted that the woman had claimed Rs 48 lakh in total compensation, bringing the complaint within its pecuniary jurisdiction under the Consumer Protection Act, 1986. The bank’s Naraina Vihar branch was in Delhi, giving the commission territorial jurisdiction as well.On the main dispute, the commission examined the bank records showing that locker rent continued to be debited from the woman’s account, including on September 25, 2018. It found that the bank had not produced a receipt establishing the locker’s surrender.The commission observed: “Even if the mistake on the part of the Opposite Party Bank was Bonafide, the Opposite Party has also failed to place on record any receipt of surrender of the locker in question”.It also found no evidence that the woman had communicated a request to surrender the locker. Nor had the bank produced a receipt showing that the jewellery or other contents had been handed over when it claimed the locker was closed.As the order states: “Further, there is no receipt of the items in the locker of the Complainant and her deceased father-in-law provided by the Opposite Party at the time of the alleged surrender of the said locker”.On that basis, the commission rejected the bank’s contention that the locker had been surrendered on May 21, 2005. It concluded that the bank had failed to establish that the woman had surrendered the locker or received its contents back. The commission held that “the belongings of the Complainant were misappropriated by the Opposite Party”.The commission directed the bank to pay Rs 47 lakh, with simple interest at 6% per annum calculated from September 1, 2018, to October 27, 2026, provided payment was made by December 27, 2026. If the bank failed to pay by that deadline, the amount would carry interest at 9% per annum from September 1, 2018, until realisation.The bank was also directed to pay Rs 3 lakh for mental agony and harassment and Rs 50,000 towards litigation costs.According to Amitraj Kaushal, Advocate at Supreme Court of India, the RBI's directions on safe deposit lockers lay down a prescribed procedure that banks must follow, including giving prior notice before terminating a locker agreement or opening a locker.Surrendering a locker is generally a formal process involving both the bank and the customer. It ordinarily requires a written request from the customer, along with the return of the locker key and an acknowledgement of the handover.“Silence from the customer is not consent. A surrender done without informing you can be challenged as deficiency in service,” he told ET.“Rent was still being debited from her account which shows the locker was live in the bank records. The Commission treated this as deficiency in service and held that the jewellery had been misappropriated by the bank,” explained Amritraj Kaushal.Keeping records of financial transactions and important agreements is essential, and a bank locker is no exception. Kaushal advised customers to retain their locker agreement and all receipts for rent payments.“Bank statements showing the rent debits were relied on by the Commission in this case so save them too.”Customers should also make it a point to visit their lockers at least once a year and maintain a record of each visit. Before placing valuables inside, they should take photographs bearing the date and keep purchase invoices or valuation documents at home rather than storing them in the locker.If a joint locker holder dies, the bank should be informed in writing and the necessary formalities completed promptly. Similarly, anyone surrendering a locker should obtain a surrender receipt signed by the bank, ensure that it mentions the date and subsequently verify that locker rent is no longer being deducted.
Article Summary: A woman held a joint locker with her father-in-law at a bank in Delhi. On September 1, 2018, the woman approached the bank to access the locker. She alleged that the bank informed her it had been surrendered on January 22, 2015. The woman claimed that jewellery worth approximately Rs 47 lakh was missing. She filed a consumer complaint in 2019, seeking the value of the jewellery.

Article Title: DLF to invest Rs 3,750 cr in JV with Everstone to buy stake in IREO India
Article Text:
DLF has partnered with the Everstone Group to create a joint venture dedicated to investing in IREO India Companies.

Sain

Real estate major DLF and Everstone Group, a Singapore-headquartered global investment manager, will form a JV to invest in IREO pvt ltd and other group companies in India (IREO India Companies) held by the IREO group of FDI funds (IREO Funds), with investments from reputed global investors. DLF intends to invest about Rs 3,750 crore for a majority stake in the JV that will hold economic interest in the IREO India companies. The proposed JV intends to invest these funds to acquire at least 20% stake in the IREO India companies, together with certain governance-related rights.Through the proposed transaction, the JV’s aggregate economic interest in the IREO India Companies will be about 40%, with the IREO Funds holding the balance. The proposed transaction could deliver developments across Delhi, Gurugram and other regions. On completion, the IREO India companies will be operated by an independent management team under the guidance of DLF and Everstone.The proposed transaction is subject to customary closing conditions, including satisfactory completion of due diligence, receipt of all applicable corporate, regulatory and third-party approvals, and execution of definitive documents.Closing is expected to occur during 2027.DLF MD Ashok Kumar Tyagi said: “We are pleased to partner with everstone group on this strategic investment. Bringing together strong industry experience and global investment capabilities, we look forward to unlocking the growth potential of the IREO India Companies.”Everstone group co-founder and CEO Sameersaid: “It’s our privilege to partner with DLF, especially given their incredible capabilities in a market they understand extremely well. Consistent with our fiduciary responsibilities we look forward to working hard and creating significant value for our IREO Funds investors.”
Article Summary: Real estate major DLF and Everstone Group will form a JV to invest in IREO India companies. DLF intends to invest about Rs 3,750 crore for a majority stake in the JV. The proposed transaction could deliver developments across Delhi, Gurugram and other regions.
